text: Mara was watching it from her window, and the snow it wasn't falling exactly, it was just coming, covering everything up, and she had felt this coming for a couple months and she felt that the sky just let it come out. By noon the town was closed, the baker put the shades down, the library closed their massive doors, even the plows were closed and they just lined up in the river bank just sitting there, with the orange lights still turning around, like some animals that are waiting. And the snow was covering everything, the traffic signs, the top of the church, the top of cars, everything just disappeared. First the sound, then the shapes. Everything just disappeared, and the street turned into just this white paper. And the elm tree across from her was wearing snow like a coat, it was just bent down. And then a crow landed on the wire, shook itself, and just became like a little black stitch in this grey. And she thought, should I call my brother, or no, and she thought no, anyway the phone just died, an hour ago, and anyway, what would she say? That the silence is louder than the city? That she stopped waiting for that car that was going to come, but it never came? She made tea, and it was just the only noise, the kettle that whistled, and she was drawing circles with her finger in the steam, and drawing circles and circles, until it just looked like two eyes, and she was looking through them, and the snow was just filling up her tracks. It was erasing it, everything she wanted to go, and she didn't cry, she just stood there until the light turned from white to blue, and then the street lamp came on, and it just made this tiny little halo of light, but it was just over snow, and she just let it burn. And the radiator was making a ticking sound, like a heart that was beating very slowly, and the tea got cold next to the blue cup that was chipped, but under all the stillness, she knew that the town is still there and she is still there.
